sanity_expectations: I_avg is finite and real over the sampled domain
I_avg >= 0 in most of the region (dominated by nonnegative E_1^2 and E_2^2 terms; interference cross-term can transiently push it slightly negative for extreme phi/theta but the sum stays bounded)
I_avg scales quadratically with a uniform rescaling E_1,E_2 -> lambda*E_1, lambda*E_2
I_avg is periodic in phi and theta with period 2*pi
Setting normalized_second_beam_centroid_offset to 0 and second_to_first_beam_waist_ratio to 1 reduces I_avg to the parent expression
excitation_report: Overall RMS of the expression is ~4.1e-3 W/m^2 (≈410*sigma), well above noise. The NEW term (E − parent) — introduced by promoting second_to_first_beam_waist_ratio from unity and by adding the centroid-offset cross-terms — has max effect ≈9.0e-4, i.e. 90.1*sigma at (E_1≈1.80, E_2≈1.95, phi≈0.17, theta≈6.13). Second_to_first_beam_waist_ratio=1.5 (inside the 1/3..3 hint) plus normalized_second_beam_centroid_offset=0.4 provide clean excitation of the new second_to_first_beam_waist_ratio-dependent factors.

theta: V->V (confirmed sampled polarization orientation axis)

rationale: Explicit closed-form for cycle- and ensemble-averaged Poynting flux; no derivatives or integrals present, so equation_type=explicit, integrator=evaluate_explicit. Inputs are the four operator-controllable knobs (E_1, E_2, phi, theta); everything else is treated as a fixed device/environment parameter. The evolution step generalized the parent by allowing (i) unequal beam waists (second_to_first_beam_waist_ratio ≠ 1) and (ii) a lateral centroid offset entering the aperture-coupled quadratic form. Setting second_to_first_beam_waist_ratio=1.5 (inside the supplied 1/3..3 hint) and normalized_second_beam_centroid_offset=0.4 excites both features while all substitutions remain finite and real. Excitation check confirms the new term contribution reaches ~90*sigma with sigma=1e-5 W/m^2 versus a dominant scale of ~4e-3 W/m^2.
